text: Moved over from Monarch Money, primarily for multi-currency support, but love so many other things about it!

After playing around, Lunch Money seems like it has the features I want & would be an absurdly helpful tool… except it’s very annoying to use on mobile. The IOS app is missing a number of features, and in order to set it up with all the customization/features I need to use the website. I wouldn’t mind this, except the website isn’t optimized for mobile and some actions are still difficult or impossible. As someone that prefer to update on-the-go, the fact that I need a laptop to do a number of things will probably be a dealbreaker. The possibilities are so good that I’m sticking it out until the end of my trial to see how impeding it actually is, but it’s just not the app I wish it was. I really wish I liked it & could recommend it to my friends.

I had mint when I lived in the US and it wasn’t my favourite but it did give me an overview of many different accounts to understand general trends in my spending and saving. For years I couldn’t find an equivalent in Canada after moving home. I ended up never feeling clear on how my finances were tracking. Lunch money is better than mint was. Very well designed and a pleasure to use.

I started using the free trial version of Lunch Money because I have a Canadian bank account, as my Monarch budgeting app stopped working and would no longer connect after several attempts. At first I thought this would be really easy to set up but I found it was actually extremely complicated. The instructions weren't super clear and all the videos I watched just made it more complicated. A person who excelled at Microsoft Excel or Microsoft programming would probably do well and really enjoy the detail that this provides but for a simple setup of a person that's quite busy, it is quite a challenge. I have since resort back to my simple google sheets version of Manual entry which is oddly easier and free.

I have used money management and budgeting apps all the way back to the Quicken and MS Money era. I watched the rise and then ruin of Mint by Intuit. 

Lunch Money is the old school simplicity and clarity of some of the originals without all the ads and junk other apps add on. Absolutely love this product and fear the day the developer sells it to a big company!

I have been using the app for almost a year now. Although I find it very user friendly and full of useful features, the connection with CIBC hasn’t been working for automatic uploads, which forces me do manually upload transactions as a CSV file, making things time consuming. I have also recently been experiencing connection issues with RBC. Lunch Money relies on a third party (Plaid) to manage connections with financial institutions. Although LM customer service people have been very responsive, if the app can’t work properly with two major Canadian banks, it makes things very frustrating and I have a hard time giving it a glowing review…

I have been having issues with the rule. Rules doesn’t work consistently and for some reason, new rules are created automatically even when I turned off the rule preferences setting. Sometimes, I have to spend more time fixing the transactions…

I’m Canadian and have been using https://lunchmoney.app/ for tracking with Plaid integrations. They have an api and I got llm to write a CLI for it. That way agent can pretty much pull the data it needs or wants. One thing I also had it do is build up a series of rules for tagging which then I run a cron for once a day. Every once in a while I just ask it to look over the rules and make new ones for uncategorized transactions. (As a side note I think having LLM “memoize” a task through a rule engine or code is really nice pattern) But once you have the cli with query you can pretty much ask the agent to do anything.
Great balance price and functionality, everything that you need! The team is doing a great job!

Fantastic platform to keep track of finances, especially transactions and merchants editing feature is super smooth! The level of customization towards analyses and statistics is outstanding and I love the multi-currency and bank-syncing features.
I’ve +10yrs finance & budgeting background myself and definitely recommend this app! Would love to see investment features (like stock tickers) in future to make this platform a comprehensive financial companion.

This product worked well until I started using wealth simple. My wealth simple accounts would constantly disconnect, and it’s always a hassle to reconnect. What’s more ridiculous is recently it started to report all the debit transactions as credits and I have to manually correct all of them. Like what?…
And every time I reach out to customer support the script is just to blame Plaid. Guess what? Monarch money seems to work just fine and they also use Plaid.
The lack of attention to this product breaking bug seems crazy to me given how popular WealthSimple is in Canada. 
Sad because I really liked this product initially but now it’s completely unusable.

Have been using this app for almost a year and really love it. I use it for expense and income tracking, but there are other features like budgeting that are likely very useful as well. I’d give it 6 stars if I could!
Great app. Sometimes the banks accounts don’t update but overall love it

I’m genuinely impressed by how streamlined, simple, and minimalist this app is. It clearly knows its role: a lightweight, on-the-go companion rather than a bloated all-in-one solution. The heavy lifting is sensibly left to the web interface on a proper desktop screen, and that focus is exactly what I’m looking for

After trying a few different apps, I was about to go back to spreadsheets when I discovered Lunch Money. It provides the multi-currency support that I need and helps me see what is actually available to spend! 

Like all financial apps, Canadian banks occasionally need to be set up again, but this seems to be more of a bank issue than an app issue. 

The user-face is aesthetically pleasing and easy to use, and the support team is responsive when you need help. 

Looking forward to future updates!
This is an excellent companion to the more extensive web app. Support is very helpful and love being a part of a discord as well as the open API structure. Good stuff LM team!

I have been waiting for a long time for an official Lunch Money mobile app, and now I am not disappointed! Especially with the refresh in v2, which has made the UI/UX even better.

It would be awesome to include more of the website data such as total net worth tab, ability to see recurring transactions, etc.

This mobile app is a companion to the web app. It has more limited functionality compared to the web app since Lunch Money is focused on a web-first experience. 

Getting started was relatively straightforward! This is a breath of fresh air compared to some money management tools that have high learning curves. 

I love that it allows for me to set certain categories to rollover funds from one budget period to the next. This is great for variable expense categories like gifts, emergency fund, sinking funds, etc. 

I also really love that you can set custom budget periods. You don’t have to follow the traditional monthly budget period if you don’t want to! You can set budget periods that align with your paycheck schedule.

Their web service for finance management is already one of the best, and this App provides a really valuable addition for simple snapshots of your accounts. It’s especially helpful for manual cash transactions as I prefer to do this on an App. NOTE: Lunch Money is already set apart from most others because they integrate multi currency accounts! I have tested many and consider LM to be similar to Wallet by Budget Bakers, Buddy Budget and Spendee (Buddy doesn’t have multi-currency yet). Spendee is a one time purchase and has a really beautiful UI, but the connection problems with certain institutions has not been worked out yet (and Wallet has even more issues with connections). If Lunch Money proves they are more stable then I will be switching from Spendee
